input.rationale: Section 1.4 (p0008-p0009) is the only grant running in our favour (access to and right to use HDI's hosting system, software and Content administration tools); the only other licence in the document (Section 6.1, p0038) is our outbound Marks licence to HDI, which benefits us and is not flagged. The Section 1.4 grant names only "the Company" — it does not extend to our affiliates or to contractors acting on our behalf, and there is no mechanism (even on written notice) to add them, so it fails the fallback on a material term. Successor transfer is adequately addressed by Section 10.3 (p0063), which makes the Agreement enforceable by and binding on successors and assigns with no consent restriction, and the grant contains no revocability-at-will language, so those elements are satisfied. The redline makes the minimal change to reach the preferred position by extending the Section 1.4 access and use rights to our affiliates and contractors and confirming they are not revocable during the term; the absence of perpetuity language is inapposite for a term hosting arrangement and is noted only.

proposal.summary: Extend the Section 1.4 access/use rights to the Company's affiliates and contractors and confirm they are not revocable at will.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the Section 1.4 access and right-to-use grant to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf (e.g. our web and IT providers), since they will need to use the hosting system and administration tools to operate the Site with us. We have also confirmed the rights are not revocable at HDI's discretion during the term; if you prefer, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice to HDI.
